item.title: 🔵 "Comment stuffing" in an HTML phishing attachment as a mechanism for evading AI-based detection?, (Fri, Jul 10th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and user awareness training.

Anyone who deals with phishing messages caught by basic security filters knows that most phishing samples tend to blend into one another, since only a small set of techniques and approaches keeps reappearing in them. That is precisely why it is worth pausing on the occasional message that does something a little out of the ordinary.

item.title: 🟠 Attackers Exploit 'Ill Bloom' Vulnerability to Drain Over $5 Million From Cryptocurrency Wallets
item.description:
Why this matters: Leadership context — useful for risk, budget, and vendor conversations.
Security firm Coinspect has disclosed a crypto wallet flaw it calls Ill Bloom, and attackers are already using it. The flaw is in how some wallet software generated its recovery phrase, the words that control the money.
